sites.evidence_type: N-terminal HA epitope; parallel surface-display screen
sites.functional_impact_measured: Surface immunostaining PME 4020.9 ± 199.4 (HA immunostaining, Tedman deep receptor scanning)
sites.rationale: Experimentally validated N-terminal HA epitope insertion (after signal-peptide cleavage where present); surface expression read out by HA immunostaining in Tedman et al. deep receptor scanning.

sources.citation: Tedman et al., Efficient experimental characterization of the GPCRome via deep receptor scanning, Nat Commun 2026 (bioRxiv 2025.09.19.677468, PMC12458215)
sources.claim: N-terminal HA epitope inserted per receptor; surface expression read out by HA immunostaining in a pooled GPCRome deep-receptor-scanning screen.

sites.evidence_type: published tag insertion in the same loop or domain
sites.functional_impact_measured: Surface display confirmed by flow cytometry with anti-V5 antibody; Wnt3a- and Wnt5a-induced reduction of surface FZD5 levels measured, demonstrating receptor-mediated endocytosis is intact and the tag does not block Wnt-induced trafficking.
sites.rationale: L5 explicitly states the V5 tag is placed 'after the signal peptide' on the amino terminus of FZD5, which by the topology landmarks means insert_after_residue=26 (last residue of the 1–26 signal peptide). Python lookup confirms residue 26 = A and residue 27 = A. The tag sits in the large extracellular N-terminal domain (residues 27–236), 210 residues from TM1, and surface display was directly confirmed by flow cytometry. The same junction is independently corroborated by HA-tagged constructs (L1–L3, L14, L15) and HiBiT-tagged constructs (L12–L13), all reporting surface-displayed full-length FZD5. HEK293A and Huh7 cells stably expressing V5-FZD5, with the V5 tag explicitly placed at the amino terminus after the signal peptide, in a pCDH lentiviral vector; full-length membrane-anchored receptor.

sources.claim: To investigate whether Wnt induces endocytosis and degradation of FZD receptors, HEK293A cells stably expressing each of the ten V5-FZDs (with the V5 tag added to the amino terminus of each FZD after the signal peptide) were treated with control, Wnt3a-conditioned or Wnt5a-conditioned medium (CM), and the FZD levels on the cell surface were examined via flow cytometry with an anti-V5 antibody.

literature_notes: The ledger supports a single extracellular tag site: the N-terminal junction after the signal peptide (insert_after_residue=26). This site is corroborated by at least 12 ledger lines using three different tag types (V5: L5, L6, L8–L11; HA: L1–L3, L14, L15; HiBiT: L12–L13). L5 is chosen as the primary clip because it is the most explicit about position ('after the signal peptide') and provides the strongest functional readout (Wnt-induced endocytosis). The C-terminal 1D4/V5 tags (L2, L6, L7, L15) are intracellular (C-tail residues 523–585) and are recorded in other_positions. The HaloTag at K439 (L4) is in ICL3 (424–450) and is also intracellular, recorded in other_positions. No ledger line supports an insertion in any extracellular loop (ECL1 292–312, ECL2 379–398, ECL3 471–501) of full-length membrane-anchored FZD5.

literature_other_positions.note: V5 tag knocked into the C-terminus of endogenous FZD5 before the stop codon via CRISPR/Cas9; the C-terminus falls in the intracellular span 523–585 and is not accessible on the extracellular face.
HaloTag inserted after K439 in the third intracellular loop (ICL3, topology span 424–450) of HA-FZD5-Nluc; tolerated but cytoplasmic, not a surface tag site.
